title: Feeding the World
objective: After this level you can explain where the world's food is grown and which crops feed the most people.
summary: Rice, maize and wheat give about 60% of the world's food energy. Rice, mostly grown in Asia-Pacific, feeds almost half of humanity. Almost half of habitable land is farmed.

cards.headline: Look at your plate. It probably started as rice, corn or wheat.
cards.body: Those three crops supply about 60% of the food energy people eat. The menu of humanity is surprisingly short, and it takes a startling amount of land.

cards.headline: A very short menu
cards.body: Just 15 crop plants provide 90% of the world's food energy. Three of them, rice, maize (corn) and wheat, supply two-thirds of that on their own: about 60% of all the energy humans eat. Bread, tortillas, noodles, porridge: the world's breakfast table is mostly variations on three plants.

cards.headline: The rice bowl
cards.body: Rice alone feeds almost half of humanity. More than 90% of the world's rice is grown and eaten in the Asia-Pacific region. Put that next to Level 91, where about 60% of people live in that same region, and it clicks: the rice fields sit right where the people are.

cards.fact: Almost half of the world's habitable land is farmed.
cards.context: And more than three-quarters of that farmland goes to livestock, for grazing and for growing animal feed. Yet meat, dairy and farmed fish supply less than a fifth of the world's calories. Most farmland, in other words, feeds animals first and people second.

questions.prompt: Which three crops supply about 60% of the world's food energy?

options.label: Potatoes, soybeans and rice
options.rationale: Only rice belongs in the top three.

options.label: Wheat, sugarcane and barley
options.rationale: Only wheat belongs in the top three.

options.label: Maize, cassava and bananas
options.rationale: Only maize belongs in the top three.

questions.explanation: Rice, maize and wheat supply two-thirds of the food energy from the 15 main crops, about 60% of the total.

questions.prompt: More than three-quarters of farmland is used for livestock. Why does that stand out?

options.label: Meat, dairy and farmed fish supply less than a fifth of calories
Livestock farming uses no land at all
options.rationale: Grazing and feed crops take most of it.

options.label: Animals only live on land nobody could farm
options.rationale: Much feed is grown on cropland.

options.label: Livestock supply most of the world's calories
options.rationale: It's the opposite: less than a fifth.

questions.explanation: Livestock take more than three-quarters of farmland, yet meat, dairy and farmed fish supply less than a fifth of calories.

questions.prompt: Farming uses almost half of habitable land. From Level 1, why is land in short supply to begin with?

options.label: Mountains cover most continents
options.rationale: Mountains matter, but the bigger fact is water.

options.label: About 71% of Earth's surface is water
Cities cover most of the land
options.rationale: Farms, not cities, take the biggest share.

questions.explanation: About 71% of Earth's surface is water, leaving only about 29% as land. Farms take almost half of the part people can live on.
